title: Perfect Stranger
full_review:
Chalk up another woeful career choice for Halle Berry, whose proven talent does not apparently extend to knowing when to say "no."

Her latest vehicle, "Perfect Stranger" (Revolution), is a patently trashy, utterly nonsensical thriller.

She plays Rowena Price, a fictitious New York newspaper's investigative reporter who, in the film's opening scene, threatens a slimy congressman who has a weakness for male interns. Her hard-won story never runs, thanks to the politician's connections, putting a damper on her barroom celebration with Miles (Giovanni Ribisi), her sleazy computer-savvy colleague.

Shortly after this disappointment, promiscuous childhood girlfriend Grace (Nicki Aycox) reaches out to Ro about exposing big-shot ad executive Harrison Hill (Bruce Willis in a nothing part) with whom she had been having an adulterous affair but who has now dumped her.

When Grace is found murdered a couple of weeks later, Ro impersonates a temp to infiltrate Hill's ad agency and prove him the killer. With Miles' help, she also impersonates one of Hill's chat-room flirtations to trap the powerful executive further with some provocative online text-messaging.

The ill-conceived script (by Todd Kornarnicki), which substitutes puerile vulgarity for intelligence, has this star reporter uttering so many gratuitous uses of the f-word that it becomes almost risible.

And never mind that events strain credulity at every turn, and most of the seamy sexual elements have little dramatic justification. James Foley, at least, directs with some visual flair.

The film contains nonstop rough and crude language and some profanity, heavy sexual content including a graphic premarital encounter without nudity, brief pornographic images, adultery, child abuse, some violent encounters including a bloody stabbing and a bludgeoning, and a gruesome morgue image. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
